title: Mutation Outcomes, Merge Policies and First-Class Conflicts
description: Every mutation must produce a diff ALONG WITH messages (level: info, warning, error, fatal). Conflicts become first-class citizens. Introduce merge policies (laissez-faire: only fatal messages prevent the merge; normal: errors and fatals prevent, warnings ignored; vigilant: any warning or worse prevents). Working alone, errors and conflicts should not arise because illegal actions are prevented up front (apps guard gestures with the same predicate the diff leaf uses). Due to the collaborative event-sourcing system and chronological merging of mutations (new order due to timestamps), errors and conflicts can always arise — e.g. one user modifies a part while another deletes it, so the modifying mutations have no effect when merged. Extend/refactor/change clean mechanisms to properly achieve this, end to end for all non-legacy technology: kernel spine (MutationOutcome/MutationMessage/MergePolicy/Conflict), derive macros, store (chronological HLC merge, quarantine + degraded conflicts, resolve accept/discard), .spr persistence, channel + TS mirror, guest SDK, Rust wasmtime host, TS browser host, React shell UI with en/de strings, hub + db authority, and the ~1400 mutation-kind diff leaves across 33 plugins. Delete the unreachable CRDT layer (📡️spr/🔀️crdt, MergeStrategyKind, ConflictRule, db ResolutionPlan) per CLAUDE.md, and rename Severity::Hint to Info repo-wide. Master plan: 📋️master-plan.md in this ticket folder (source: /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/all-mutations-must-produce-hidden-bubble.md). Workforce: one Opus 5 coordinator agent, Sonnet 5 lane executors, Haiku 4.5 read-only scouts/auditors (the llm field records sonnet-5 because the registry has no Claude-5 Opus/Fable value).
summary:
Every mutation now produces a diff ALONG WITH messages. `Mutation::diff`/`MutationKind::diff` return `MutationOutcome<D>{diff, messages}` where each `MutationMessage` carries `{level: Severity{Info,Warning,Error,Fatal}, code, message, target, op_index}`; `validate` is deleted from `Mutation`/`MutationKind`/`CompositeMutationKind` so a check can no longer be silently skipped. Exactly seven gate-enforced codes: mutation.target-missing (Error), mutation.no-op / mutation.partial / mutation.clamped (Warning), mutation.duplicate-id / mutation.invariant (Fatal), mutation.cascade (Info). Enforced invariants: Fatal => empty diff, Error => empty diff, messages deterministic in (op, base).

Merge policies `MergePolicy{LaissezFaire, Normal (default), Vigilant}`: LaissezFaire rejects only Fatal, Normal rejects Error+Fatal, Vigilant rejects Warning+. A rejected local dispatch is refused atomically (nothing applied, nothing recorded, typed `VcsError::Rejected{policy, messages}`), so working alone the UI prevents illegal actions and the store refuses them.

Conflicts are first-class: new `spr/conflict` module with `Conflict{id,kind,status,messages,actors,timestamp}`, `ConflictKind::{Quarantined{policy,envelopes}, Degraded{edit_ids}}`, `ConflictStatus`, `ConflictResolution::{Accept,Discard}`, `EditMessages`, `DispatchReport`, `MergeReport`; persisted in .spr via `HistoryConflict` + `HistoryOpMeta.messages`. `ingest_remote` now merges CHRONOLOGICALLY by HLC: it sorts the batch, splices it at its timestamp position, re-evaluates the whole affected suffix (including local edits invalidated by a newly inserted earlier edit), applies the policy to the worst level, and either accepts (opening a Degraded conflict when work was lost) or quarantines the batch as an open conflict resolvable with Accept/Discard. Forward ops and MutationMeta are never rewritten; only diffs, inverses and messages are recomputed. The dev's example holds: A modifies a part while B deletes it earlier by timestamp => A's modification yields mutation.target-missing with an empty diff.

The CRDT layer is deleted per CLAUDE.md: spr/crdt, MergeStrategyKind, ConflictRule, merge_concurrent_diffs, db ResolutionPlan, Mutation::{merge_strategy,conflict_rule,reconcile}, ReconcileReport/ReconcileSeverity, SpaceConflict, assert_crdt_* — zero residue. Severity is now the single level vocabulary (Hint renamed to Info, order reversed so derive(Ord) is the level order).

Landed end to end for all non-legacy technology: kernel spine, both derive-macro mirror files, store, .spr persistence, channel (CHANNEL_VERSION 10->11, AppCommand 30/31/32, AppFrame 23/24, extended Invocation/Error) plus the TS mirror with matching tags, guest SDK, Rust wasmtime host, TS browser host, React shell (Conflicts panel, rejected-dispatch toast, feed tones, history level badges, merge-policy setting) with en+de strings, and hub + db authority (SubmitOptions.policy, outcome-gated pipeline rejecting before any WAL append). About 1430 diff leaves across 33 plugins were converted with real verb-family messages.

Verification actually executed: `verify mutation-outcome-law` passes with 0 breaches (was 182) across seven new policy gates wired into `verify gate`, with launch.json entries and an nx target; cargo tests 987/0 (os-kernel), 137/0 (framework), 43/0 (plugin-host incl. a wasmtime e2e policy test), 424/0 (db), 15/0 (run); 21/33 plugin crates check clean and the remaining 29 errors are foreign (verified to not mention this ticket's vocabulary); real wasm32-wasip2 builds green for dag/cad/process3d+4 extensions/trinity/writer; TS suites at baseline.

Real defects found and fixed beyond the migration: chronological determinism did not hold (arrival order decided the outcome, and conflict ids leaked the ticking store clock); WorkflowMutation remove-inverses restored cascades before the node existed; the DSL value codec could not round-trip newtype-wrapped scalars and silently dropped tuple-variant fields; a ghost edit id was silently skipped during replay; ConflictId could be minted from an empty id list; the conflict list grew unbounded; 15 wasm-gated sites were broken and invisible to native checks; the merge-policy control was wire-dead and remote-origin merge reports were dropped before reaching the UI.

Known gaps, stated honestly in the final summary: no live browser click-through proof (dev server could not stay up under this ticket's own concurrent cargo load; policy enforcement is proven at the host layer by a wasmtime e2e test and in the shell by vitest); 12 plugin crates still fail on foreign errors owned by the live FULL-STDIO, viewer/editor-split and UI tickets; and 116 gltf diff leaves are a separate architecture owned by FULL-STDIO, recorded in a documented shrink-only gate allowlist.
